title: Telemetry batch ingestion with enrichment and sink
name: Telemetry ingest service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code bounds the time spent waiting on its downstream dependencies? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The calibration service starts responding in 400ms instead of 20ms. What is the effect on ingestion?
choices: Batches take 400ms longer per reading, because timeouts are only logged
The calibration call is retried until it responds within the limit
The whole batch fails with a TimeoutException and is retried
Affected readings are enriched with offset 0.0 and marked stale after the 150ms timeout, and the batch continues

questions.prompt: The time-series sink fails with a timeout partway through writing a batch. What does the consumer do next?
choices: Waits one second without committing, so the batch is delivered again, which means the sink must tolerate duplicates
Commits the batch anyway so the stream is not blocked
Terminates the stream and the process exits
Splits the batch and writes each half separately

questions.prompt: Readings with a deviceId that the registry does not know are handled by which path?
choices: They fail the batch, since the registry returns an error
They are written with a default site and stale = true
They are dropped from the batch before writing, and counted by a metric whose value is the number of dropped readings
They are retried through the calibration fallback
